newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU adopts action plan on satellite communications.
newsitem.headline: EU adopts action plan on satellite communications.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it would work with industry to promote the European Union's increasingly critical satellite communications sector.
"A strong and coherent satellite communications industry and services sector is of high economic and political importance for Europe," it said in a statement.

Expressing concern about U.S. dominance of the sector, the Commission said it had adopted a plan calling for a "public- private partnership" between the Commission, national governments and companies.
The plan calls for action to enforce relevant EU regulations, strengthen Europe's presence in international bodies, review technical standards work and boost space research.
"Should Europe not react in a coordinated manner, there is a high risk from being kept out of the most promising market segments," it said.

The initiative covers personal communications systems -- which will offer voice, data and fax services to small inexpensive terminals -- and high-capacity broadband systems that will transmit multimedia applications and are expected to play an important role in advanced Internet access.
The revenues generated by those systems are expected to reach $400 billion over the next 10 years, the Commission said.
The Commission noted in a background paper issued in December that the U.S. industry had already launched proposals for global satellite communications systems worth $50 billion.
Those included Teledesic, a joint venture involving Microsoft Corp chairman Bill Gates.
The Commission's action plan says that some EU laws, for example a directive liberalising satellite communications services and equipment, have not been implemented properly in some countries.
It said it would ask industry to provide regular information on barriers to introducing satellite communications systems and services and propose new regulations if needed.
It said it would also ask the European Conference of Postal and Telecommunications Administrations (CEPT) to speed up work on harmonising conditions for national authorisations of satellite systems.
The Commission said it would conduct an in-depth analysis of international trade policy questions and propose ways to coordinate EU positions in international bodies.

It said it would also identify possible research cooperation between the EU, the European Space Agency, industry and national governments and may propose EU research funding in the area of terrestrial/satellite, or "multimode", terminals. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
